provider: NASA Langley Research Center - POWER Project
data_kind_note: NASA POWER meteorology is reanalysis output (MERRA-2 / GEOS-IT assimilation models), averaged over a ~0.5 x 0.625 degree grid cell. It is a model-based estimate constrained by observations, not a direct ground or satellite measurement.
methodology_summary: Meteorological parameters derived from NASA GMAO MERRA-2 reanalysis (1981-01-01 to about one month behind real time) and GEOS-IT (near real time, ~2 day latency). Native resolution 0.5 deg lat x 0.625 deg lon. Daily values aggregated in Local Solar Time. NASA POWER recommends ending climate-trend analyses about 2 months behind near real time, because MERRA-2 values replace GEOS-IT values as they become available.
spatial_resolution: 0.5 deg latitude x 0.625 deg longitude (native MERRA-2 grid)
fill_value_handling: values equal to header.fill_value replaced with NaN; no imputation; no zero-fill

T2M.definition: The average air (dry bulb) temperature at 2 meters above the surface of the earth.

PRECTOTCORR.definition: The average MERRA-2 bias corrected total precipitation at the surface of the earth.

processing_history.detail: HTTP GET request_url; response bytes stored unmodified
JSON parsed; dates interpreted as YYYYMMDD in time_standard
continuity, duplicates, units, plausibility flags (no values altered)

warnings: T2M: 2 trailing missing days (expected near-real-time latency)
PRECTOTCORR: 2 trailing missing days (expected near-real-time latency)

citation: The data was obtained from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Langley Research Center (LaRC) Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resource (POWER) Project funded through the NASA Earth Science Division.
citation_data_reference: Data obtained from the POWER Project's Daily API v2.10.3 on 2026-11-14.
